issue_context.title: BUG: File saved with to_stata and version=119 cannot be opened with STATA 15.1 SE
issue_context.body:
- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.

- [ ] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.

---

**Note**: Please read [this guide](https://matthewrocklin.com/blog/work/2018/02/28/minimal-bug-reports) detailing how to provide the necessary information for us to reproduce your bug.

#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example

```python
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({"A":[1]})
df.to_stata("a.dta", version=119)

```

#### Problem description

I have Stata/SE 15.1.

I run the above code, then try to open `a.dta` with my version of Stata.

But Stata doesn't open the file and instead gives the following error:

> dataset too large
>     This .dta file format was created by Stata/MP and has more variables than your Stata can handle.

Of course the file is not too large, since it contains only 1 observation and 1 variable.
It looks like pandas is saving the file in the "MP" version. 
I propose to save it in the SE version, or at least specify which sub-version of Stata the file is saved in in the documentation.

comments:
The files we create are compliant with the state DTA documentation.  It is hard to know what is broken.  I think 119 can never be opened in SE since it is only created when there is a very large number of variables.  Stata will only create 118 files for datasets that SE can handle. 

IMO there is no fix possible that can address this limitation imposed by Stata Corp. 

> It looks like pandas is saving the file in the "MP" version.

Just to be 100% clear, there is _only_ an MP version of 119 since it can only be created by Stata MP (officially).

I would be happy to support a PR that added some documentation that states that 119 cannot be opened in Stata SE. Although this might need a caveat as to the date since this might change in the future, which makes documenting Stata's behavior a bit problematic.

review_comments:
I wouldn't say "for now". Something along the lines of

"Version 119 should usually only be used when the number of variables exceeds the capacity of dta format 118. Exporting smaller datasets in format 119 may have unintended consequences, and, as of November 2020, Stata SE cannot read version 119 files. "

Thanks,

I copied your suggestion verbatim.
